claims.text: Thermomechanical processing can develop a dual-phase microstructure with homogeneous, coherent nanoprecipitates in the target refractory high-entropy alloy.
Such a dual-phase nanoprecipitate microstructure will improve ductility and uniform deformability.
The improvement in ductility and uniform deformability will occur without sacrificing high strength.
The treatment will preserve impact-induced energy release.
The untreated starting material is an as-cast, single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy.
Hot rolling followed by annealing can induce a dual-phase structure containing finely dispersed, coherent nanoprecipitates.
The proposed effect should hold under ambient and dynamic impact loading and at service-relevant temperatures.
The treated microstructure will contain coherent nanoprecipitates uniformly distributed in the matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as deformable obstacles to dislocation motion.
Deformable nanoprecipitates mitigate stress concentrations.
Deformable nanoprecipitates promote more uniform dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitate-mediated deformation mechanism enhances ductility and uniform deformation.
The proposed microstructure preserves mechanisms responsible for high strength.
The proposed microstructure preserves mechanisms responsible for rapid release of stored energy under impact.
Relative to the as-cast control, the treated alloy will have greater uniform elongation.
Relative to the as-cast control, the treated alloy will have enhanced impact deformability.
Relative to the as-cast control, the treated alloy will retain high yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
The untreated as-cast alloy has limited ductility and less uniform deformation under dynamic loading.
The proposed effect applies generally to refractory high-entropy alloys used in energetic structural applications.
The treatment may not transfer to substantially different alloy compositions, temperatures, or strain-rate regimes.
